description: System prompt rendering shared by pkg-r and pkg-py. The source is tests/shared/prompt-render.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

render.description: Each case renders prompts/system-prompt.md with `data` and compares the result to the file named by `expected`, resolved next to this fixture. `data` is the whole mapping the renderer receives, so a case exercises the template and the renderer, not the code that assembles the mapping. Expected output is a Markdown file rather than an escaped string so a reviewer can read the prompt the agent would receive.
rules: Substituted values are inserted literally, never rendered again.
Runs of blank lines collapse to one, and the result is trimmed.

template_render.description: Small templates rendered on their own, rather than the shipped prompt, for forms the prompt does not use today but that both renderers have to agree on. Jinja2 lets a tag span lines, so a renderer that scans line by line would emit the tag as text while the other renders it.

cases.name: tag and value split across lines
text after a raw region

tool_data.description: Prompt data derived from the names of the tools an agent registered. `has_*` drives the citable and non-citable lists in the template; `citation_trust_exception` is a clause spliced into a sentence, so it carries its own leading space and is empty when no trusted-calculation tool is registered.

that is not based solely on output from `call_calculation`

unsupported.description: Jinja2 is much larger than the subset both renderers implement, so a template using anything outside it has to be rejected by both. Otherwise a change to the shared template renders in Python and fails in R. Each case supplies data that would be valid if the construct were supported, so what is under test is the syntax and not a missing value.

cases.name: loops
elif
expression conditions
a loop whose tag spans lines

malformed.description: Templates that use only the supported tags but put them together in a way neither renderer can make sense of. Jinja2 raises on all of these, so the R renderer has to as well: a template that fails in one package must fail in the other rather than rendering some branch of its own choosing. Each package raises its own language's error, so a case asserts rejection rather than a message.

cases.name: a second else in one if

rejected_data.description: Data both renderers must reject. Names are checked before rendering rather than when a branch is taken, so a value missing from a section that is switched off still fails. Checking lazily would hide it in one package until a later change switched the section on. Each package raises its own language's error, so a case asserts rejection rather than a message.

cases.name: missing value in a disabled branch
missing condition in a disabled branch
condition that is not a flag
value that is not a string
